title: Maximum Team Size with Overlapping Intervals
summary: Given two arrays startTime and endTime, each of length n, where startTime[i] is the start time and endTime[i] is the end time for the i-th employee.
statement: Given two arrays startTime and endTime, each of length n, where startTime[i] is the start time and endTime[i] is the end time for the i-th employee. A team is valid if there is at least one employee who can interact with every other member. The task is to find the maximum size of such a valid team.
constraints: startTime and endTime have equal positive length and startTime[i]≤endTime[i].
A team is valid when one member’s interval overlaps every other member’s interval.
Return the maximum valid team size.
reference_solution:
def maximum_interval_team(start_time,end_time):
    from bisect import bisect_left,bisect_right
    intervals=list(zip(start_time,end_time));starts=sorted(start_time);ends=sorted(end_time);answer=0
    for left,right in intervals:
        ending_before=bisect_left(ends,left);starting_by=bisect_right(starts,right)
        answer=max(answer,starting_by-ending_before)
    return answer

hints: Fix the member who overlaps everyone else.
For anchor [l,r], exclude intervals ending before l and starting after r.
Sorted endpoint arrays and binary search count the remaining intervals in logarithmic time.
An interval survives exactly when it intersects the anchor, so the largest anchor count is precisely the largest valid team.
